title: Whole-exome sequencing of normal lung tissues, precursor lesions and invasive lung adenocarcinomas
summary: Understanding cellular processes underlying early lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) development is needed to devise intervention strategies. Here, we performed whole exome sequencing (WES) of human treatment-naive lungs comprising various stages in the sequence of pathogenesis of LUAD including normal lung tissues, atypical adenomatous hyperplasia (AAH), adenocarcinoma in situ (AIS), minimally invasive adenocarcinoma (MIA) and LUAD.
overall_design:
WES of tissues was performed on DNA isolated from formalin-fixed paraffin embedded tissues using the TWIST-WES protocol. Sequencing was done on the NovaSeq 6000 platform from Illumina.

Raw files for human/patient samples were not submitted to GEO due to concerns about submitting personally identifiable sequence data for open access.

title: Lung tissue with AAH of patient 1 [WES]
characteristics_ch1: cell line: Formalin-fixed paraffin embedded human lung tissue
data_processing:
WES experiment: Reads were mapped to the human reference genome GRCh38 (hg38) using BWA-mem. Duplicates were marked for filtering and base quality scores were recalibrated using GATK61. Somatic single nucleotide variants and indels were called using MuTect2 with default settings followed by post-calling filtering, and they were subsequently annotated using GATK Funcotator and ANNOVAR. The following criteria were applied to filter variants: (i) only variants marked as "PASS" by MuTect2 were considered; (ii) a minimum coverage of 10× for normal samples and 20× for non-normal samples (AAH, AIS, MIA and LUAD) was required; (iii) variants were required to have at least 4 alternate reads or a variant allele frequency (VAF) of ≥5% in the non-normal regions, while having fewer than 3 alternate reads and a VAF of <5% in the corresponding normal regions, and a VAF ratio (normal/non-normal) of <0.2; (iv) only variants with a median distance of at least 5 bases from the read ends were considered; (v) common variants reported by gnomAD (the Genome Aggregation Database, https://gnomad.broadinstitute.org/), Phase-3 1000 Genome Project (http://phase3browser.1000genomes.org/Homo_sapiens/Info/Index) or the NHLBI GO Exome Sequencing Project (ESP6500) (http://evs.gs.washington.edu/EVS/) with minor allele frequencies greater than 0.5% were removed. Somatic mutations located within introns, untranslated regions (UTRs), UTR-flanking regions, or those classified as silent mutations were also excluded from subsequent analyses. The somatic mutation burden for each sample was calculated based on 3 major mutation types (missense, truncating, and in-frame indels), as previously described.
Assembly: GRCh38
Supplementary files format and content: text files of mutation calling reults
